author: sonnet
label: c2-nat-sonnet-01
changes: Step 3 and step 8: a crash between reserve and provider call is now recovered by step 8, which re-sends refunds with no provider id after 5 minutes (was: wait for the 1 hour check).
Step 4: stated that the call runs inline in the web request, with a spinner and a worst case of about 45 seconds.
Step 8: the 1-hour wait is now measured from created_at, and the selection is split into refunds with and without a provider id.

Steps 5 and 6: clarified that a 4xx on a create call is a direct rejection handled by step 6, and step 9 is the single path for final results of accepted refunds. Step 6 now locks the row and only fails it if still pending.
Data model and steps 1, 9, 11: the order's refund label is computed on read from succeeded refunds, not stored, because payments is unchanged.
Data model and step 7: the webhook_events row is inserted with processed_at null, and only a set processed_at counts as done, so redelivery after a not-found refund is processed.
Step 10: named the worker (a background worker in our app, checking every minute) and a 15-minute stale-claim time, and listed both as our own choices in the open questions.
Step 5: noted that pending is the normal state and the admin sees the final state when the webhook or poll reports it.
Step 4: stated that the 24-hour key window is the provider's rule and that we count it from created_at, because the brief does not say from which call it counts (Q9).

Step 5: said that a 2xx in step 4 runs step 5 in the same request and the admin sees 'Refund pending' (Q10); made the provider_refund_id save conditional on it being null so overlapping sends are harmless (Q11).
Step 8: added that overlapping sends are harmless because of the same key and the idempotent save, and that the poller passes the provider message for failed refunds to step 9 (Q11, Q12).
Steps 7 and 9: pass the failure message to step 9, which stores it in provider_message when it sets failed; the assumptions now say the payload and get-refund response carry it (Q12).
Step 11: said the page does not refresh itself and the admin reloads (Q13).
Step 3: said what the admin does after a 409 and that the form gets a new client_request_id (Q14).
Step 10: put the stale-claim condition into the claim UPDATE and said who releases the claim on failure and on a crash (Q15).
Open questions: added the unknown start of the provider's 24-hour key window.

Step 3: added a lookup by client_request_id right after the payment lock, returning the existing refund. Two identical simultaneous requests now resolve cleanly instead of the second hitting a unique-constraint error. Steps renumbered inside step 3.
Step 2: stated that a reused client_request_id returns the existing refund with its current state, does not call the provider and creates nothing, and that step 3 repeats the check under the lock.
Step 3 and step 4: said where the charge id comes from (the payment row, read under the lock, already stored by the existing system).
Data model: noted that existing payments already stores the charge id, captured amount and status.
Open questions: added that the exact charge id column name on payments is not known to the plan.
Replaced the opening line with a short summary (what it is, how the flow goes, why) and added the state of the old process (dashboard refunds not recorded).

Added a Terms section: provider, captured, refund status, cap, remaining amount, idempotency key, row lock, webhook, poller, outbox, order refund label, audit entry. Moved the 24-hour key-window explanation from step 4 into the idempotency key term.

Added a short 'Rules that apply to every step' list (permission, reason list, retry/4xx rule, 24-hour check, email once) so brief requirements are stated once instead of repeated across steps; step 4 now points to it for the retry limit.
Moved the order refund label definition (computed on read) out of the data model into Terms and removed the repeat of it in steps 9 and 11.
Moved the existing payments description and the 'no refund table yet' fact into the data model intro.
Cut the repeated 'browser never contacts the provider' line from step 2 (kept in Terms) and the 'out-of-order handled by step 2 above' failure bullet in step 9 (already in its step 2).
Trimmed small repetitions: the 'do not change order status' wording in step 6, the 'retry up to 3 more times' restatement in step 4, and the charge-id aside in step 4.
Renamed 'Assumptions and open questions' to 'Open questions' and placed it last, as the layout requires; kept every assumption and open item.

Kept all numbers, limits, columns, constraints and step content from the first version, including the changes made in the rounds (inline call, 5-minute re-send, computed label, processed_at handling, stale-claim condition, client_request_id check under the lock).
